key_insight: Combining physics-based simulation and neural networks identified an optimal tested HDPE friction stir welding condition of 1500 rpm, 30 mm/min and 60 °C bottom preheating.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports process-window selection for reducing weld defects and stabilizing thermal and axial-force responses in HDPE joining.
method: Develop a 3D Coupled Eulerian–Lagrangian model to simulate temperature, force, material flow and defects.
Train two multilayer perceptron neural networks on experimental temperature and axial-force data.
Use simulation and neural-network predictions to map defective and defect-free welding windows.
evidence_signal: The experimentally validated CEL model reproduced weld defects and thermomechanical responses; ANN predictions achieved R² of 0.91–0.99, while 60 °C preheating reduced peak plunge force from 1600 N to approximately 1100 N.
watch_item: Reported ANN generalization is limited to the tested parameter space; predictions outside it require additional experimental validation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
